name: Bill

temperament.summary: Meek, willing, slow on the uptake and easily flustered; the good-natured underling who gets every job and every knock. Never resentful.
temperament.baseline: Diligent and dutiful; waits to be told.
temperament.under_pressure: Goes limp and dazed, mouth open, unable to act; then keeps at the job with whatever is to hand.

traits.description: Everyone hands everything to Bill: the other ladder, the chimney. He goes without protest.

evidence.note: 'Bill’s got the other—Bill! fetch it here, lad!' Then he is picked to go down the chimney.
Alice: 'they seem to put everything upon Bill!'

traits.description: He cannot make out what happened to him, whether it is being kicked out of the chimney, losing his pencil or being set in the jury-box upside down.

evidence.note: 'a deal too flustered to tell you'; 'up I goes like a sky-rocket!'
Could not make out at all what had become of his pencil.
Too overcome to do anything but sit with his mouth open, gazing at the roof.

traits.description: Keeps trying to do his duty with whatever he has left: writes with a finger, then with the ink running down his face.

evidence.note: Writes with one finger for the rest of the day though it leaves no mark.
Hastily starts again using the ink trickling down his face.

traits.description: Even just after the blow he thanks his carers and says he is better, with no anger at whoever kicked him.

evidence.note: 'No more, thank ye; I’m better now'.

motivation.core: To do what he is told and do it properly, whether the job is ladder, chimney or juror's slate.
motivation.fear: Failing at a task he has been given, and confusion he cannot account for.
motivation.wants_from_alice: Nothing. He hardly knows she is the cause of his troubles.

shifts.from: odd-job hand of the White Rabbit's household (ch004)
shifts.to: sworn juror at the trial, anxious to record everything

habits.habit: Answers to his name at once and goes where he is sent
When something goes wrong, freezes with his mouth open, staring upward
Hunts all about for a lost thing before settling for a poor substitute
A lean, sinuous way of moving: slides along walls and benches, flattens to squeeze through tight places
habits.reason: The source gives no gait. Natural lizard locomotion for the photoreal CGI lizard (SUP-002 as amended by BIB-0027), which also suits his chimney job.

decision_pattern: Does not decide; he complies. When the means fail, he improvises the humblest workaround rather than complain or ask.

taboos.taboo: Never refuses an order or talks back to those above him
Never blames anyone for his mishaps
Never abandons a task; he carries on however useless the means

facade.reason: Transparent, simple character; no hidden self in the source.

waking_life_embodiment.embodies: Not an authority but its object: the lowest servant of a household (the boot-boy or garden lad called 'lad' and sent up ladders and down chimneys), the one who carries every order down the chain.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: The servants and farm hands around the family house and the neighbouring farm, whom Alice sees taking orders all day.
waking_life_embodiment.authority_trait: The underside of authority: the obedient underling who absorbs everyone's commands and knocks.
waking_life_embodiment.coming_of_age_reading: Bill is where Alice first uses power herself, without much thought. She kicks him out of the chimney (ch004-p26), takes his squeaking pencil (ch011-p09) and puts him back head-down (ch012-p04). Her flicker of care ('the poor little thing') is the start of noticing the people beneath her, the reverse of the adult authority she is learning to resist.
waking_life_embodiment.reason: His servant role and Alice's treatment of him are sourced. Mapping him to the waking household's lowest servant is a design reading consistent with ruling 5.3 B (housemaid doubling) and the farm setting.

performance_baseline: Photoreal CGI lizard (SUP-002, BIB-0027): small, willing, eager-eyed; comic through total earnestness. Quick head-cocks when given an order, throat pulsing while he waits, a dazed sprawl with splayed toes after the chimney. Always the one clinging to the ladder. Pathos, never slapstick cruelty.
